title: fix: keep custom model routes on their declared tool surface
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Custom model endpoints could inherit the standard catalog endpoint's compatibility flags. Inherited Code Mode preference could suppress Tool Search even when the custom endpoint did not support the same tool behavior. Config materialization and runtime resolution now use the endpoint that owns those capabilities.

## User Impact

Catalog capabilities apply to their matching API and physical endpoint. Equivalent Anthropic `/v1` and `/v1/` spellings retain the canonical endpoint's capabilities. When configuration selects catalog endpoint A after discovery returned endpoint B, resolution selects A's catalog capabilities, including provider-only overlays with no model row. Same-endpoint discovery keeps its refreshed metadata.

**Upgrade note:** Custom endpoints that implicitly borrowed `codeMode: "preferred"` now use the normal Tool Search controls. An endpoint verified to support Code Mode can retain the existing explicit `models.providers.<provider>.models[].compat.codeMode: "preferred"` setting. Other endpoint-specific flags, including `supportsTemperature`, also belong in the custom endpoint's existing `compat` declaration. No new configuration field is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep compatibility decisions at the existing catalog and transport owners. Reuse Anthropic endpoint normalization and consult the existing static catalog lookup only when discovery's endpoint differs from the selected endpoint. Doctor retains its unique-route and equality checks when removing redundant compatibility declarations; divergent and custom declarations remain protected.

Related: #154964, whose Gateway/MCP proof exposed the original defect.

## Evidence

- The route-alias and discovery-to-configured-route failures were reproduced at the resolver boundary. The provider-only regression also failed for missing capabilities on raw and materialized configuration, with retained-discovery and same-route refresh controls passing.
- All 332 candidate tests passed: 15 route cases, 4 catalog cases, 21 config-default cases, 24 migration cases, and 268 sibling cases. Measured command wall with one worker: route file 29.081 seconds, catalog 1.544 seconds, defaults 16.303 seconds, and migration 17.770 seconds. The four unchanged sibling files passed together in 55.382 seconds. [Focused proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35968448656).
- Fresh independent P2 review found no actionable issues. The only subsequent change was the exact assertion allowance shrink from seven to six, leaving production and test bytes unchanged.
- All mapped checks passed in 1,570.165 seconds, including all 25 core-test typecheck graphs. Canonical package build and validation passed in 379.273 seconds. [Checks and package proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35972378056).

The [published-updater proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35989001093) passed on the unchanged candidate tree. The released `2026.9.4` updater installed the canonical `2026.9.5` candidate and ran its Doctor. Before any manual Doctor invocation, the original config's exact `.pre-update` backup was verified, only the matching canonical compatibility declaration was removed, divergent temperature and custom-endpoint Code Mode declarations were preserved, and the selected model stayed unchanged. Two subsequent Doctor passes retained identical config bytes. The complete installed-update cell took 85.309 seconds; the updater command itself took 48.401 seconds. This used isolated state and `--no-restart`, with the updater's own staged validation and canary. Installed model status proves selection; the resolver tests prove compatibility behavior. The initial fixture failure was an incorrect expectation that postinstall retained its consumed lifecycle marker; it was corrected without changing product code, and all other packaged-file hashes remained checked.

[Current-head CI35977015261](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35977015261) passed for `dd15d1a17c35b499b2c4d400ad5a0f18e10ec313` (140 successful jobs; 16 skipped). In CI, summed reported case times were 0.053 seconds for the 15 route cases, 0 milliseconds at reporter precision for the 4 catalog cases, 0.002 seconds for the 21 defaults cases, and 0.373 seconds for the 24 migration cases. These exclude file setup/import/teardown; CI file wall times were not available. The standalone file walls above remain the measured total command costs.

Earlier composed Gateway/MCP proof for the original route fix passed with four tool-bearing requests exercising Tool Search, description, and the real MCP call. That proof predates the added alias and discovery cases; its temporary fixture overlay is excluded from this PR. Earlier CI35798278130 failed plugin-state and session-group fixtures; the reproduced failures were repaired by [8ce411c1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8ce411c1aedf128cd63f46189eb1204c3a0d9fc1) and [46dfea6a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/46dfea6a42010c942345d684b6dc23752d1f2cbe), both already included in this branch. CI35806084181 passed on the previous head `355ca68a`; those historical results are not presented as current-head CI.
